# Work order: Workover - ESP replacement, W-17

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| WO number | WO-048 |
| Event reference | EV-0094 |
| Well | W-17 (Wadi Field, vertical, ESP) |
| Category | Maintenance |
| Priority | High |
| Raised | 2026-03-08 |
| Planned start | 2026-03-10 |
| Completion | 2026-03-17 |
| Status | Closed |

## Scope of work
Replace the failed ESP on W-17 following the ESP trip on 2026-03-04 (EV-0092: motor overload, phase current imbalance, low insulation resistance on megger test). Mobilize workover rig, pull the existing completion, replace pump, motor and cable, run back and restore production.

## Safety and permits
- Permit to Work issued under SOP-HSE-005 Permit to Work for Workover and Rig Operations.
- Well killed and barriers verified before pulling the string.
- Pre-job safety meeting held with rig crew, ESP vendor and Lead Operator.

## Materials
- Varenta VL-538 pump, serial 2M-1187-044 (batch 2M-1187)
- New ESP power cable
- Standard consumables and cable clamps

## Execution notes and close-out remarks
- Workover rig mobilized and work started 2026-03-10.
- Pulled ESP serial 7Q-0419-112 (batch 7Q-0419), which had run 13 months.
- Teardown found motor winding insulation breakdown and light scale on the pump stages.
- Installed new Varenta VL-538, serial 2M-1187-044 (batch 2M-1187), with new cable.
- Work completed 2026-03-17. Well returned to production on 2026-03-18.
- Total downtime recorded: 192 hours.

## Production check
| Period | Days | Oil (bbl/d) | Gas (Mscf/d) | Water cut (%) | GOR (scf/bbl) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (to 2026-03-09) | 8 | 1203 | 928.8 | 32.6 | 772 |
| After restart (to 2026-03-24) | 6 | 1288 | 1029.9 | 32.7 | 800 |

Water cut is essentially unchanged. Oil rate is higher after restart. Production Engineer to continue monitoring ESP parameters. Work order closed.

# Incident note: ESP trip on W-17

**Document ID:** IN-032
**Note date:** 2026-03-09
**Event ID:** EV-0092
**Well:** W-17 (Wadi Field, vertical, ESP)
**Severity:** High
**Status at note date:** Closed
**Prepared by:** Production Engineer

## What happened
On 2026-03-04 the ESP on W-17 tripped on motor overload with phase current imbalance. The installed pump is a Varenta VL-538, serial 7Q-0419-112 (batch 7Q-0419), with a run life of 13 months.

## Immediate actions
- Restart attempts were made by the operations team and all failed.
- A megger test on the motor showed low insulation resistance.
- The well was shut in and held shut in pending workover.
- The Production Supervisor and Workover Supervisor were informed.

## Findings so far
The electrical readings point to a motor fault. Downhole inspection is only possible once the pump is pulled, so the root cause is not yet confirmed.

## Impact
- Event period: 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-09.
- Downtime as of the note date: 144 hours.
- Production on 2026-03-04 was 0 bbl oil, 0 Mscf gas and 0 hours uptime.
- Rates in the 7 days to 2026-03-03 averaged 1198.5 bbl/d oil, 925.4 Mscf/d gas, 32.6% water cut and GOR 772 scf/bbl. Deferred oil is estimated from this baseline, about 1198.5 bbl for each day of downtime.

## Status
The incident record is closed at the note date. The well remains shut in. A workover to replace the ESP is planned to start on 2026-03-10 (EV-0094) and is tracked under its own maintenance event. Return-to-production timing will be confirmed after the workover.

## Next actions
1. Workover Supervisor to confirm the rig and the ESP vendor crew for 2026-03-10.
2. Field Engineer to request a teardown inspection of the pulled equipment.
3. Production Engineer to review the restart conditions and set the post-workover startup plan.
4. Lead Operator to keep the wellhead isolated and log checks until the rig arrives.

## Reference
SOP-OPS-001 ESP Trip Response and Restart.

**Document ID:** WT-016
**Well:** W-17 (Wadi Field, vertical, ESP)
**Test date:** 2026-03-23
**Procedure:** SOP-OPS-004 Well Test Procedure with the Mobile Test Separator

## Test conditions
- Duration: 24 hours
- Choke: 48/64 in
- Flowing wellhead pressure: 445 psi
- Installed ESP: Varenta VL-538, pump serial 2M-1187-044 (batch 2M-1187), installed 2026-03-17
- Well status: producing

| Parameter | Result |
|---|---|
| Oil | 1281 bbl/d |
| Gas | 1036.2 Mscf/d |

# Incident note: ESP failure on W-27

**Document ID:** IN-057
**Note date:** 2026-08-22
**Event:** EV-0150
**Well:** W-27 (Wadi Field, horizontal, ESP)
**Severity:** High
**Status at note date:** Closed

## What happened
On 2026-08-18 the ESP on W-27 tripped on motor overtemperature. A restart attempt then tripped on ground fault. Insulation resistance measured on the motor was below the minimum acceptable value. The installed pump is a Varenta VL-538, pump serial 7Q-0419-086 (batch 7Q-0419), with a run life of 11 months. The well was shut in pending workover.

## Immediate actions
- The well was kept shut in after the ground fault trip, and no further restarts were attempted.
- The drive was isolated and the surface cable and connections were checked.
- The Production Supervisor and the Workover Supervisor were informed.

## Findings so far
- The overtemperature trip followed by a ground fault at restart, together with low motor insulation resistance, points to a motor electrical failure.
- The cause of the failure will be confirmed when the unit is pulled and inspected.

## Impact
- Downtime: 120 hours from 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-22.
- Production on 2026-08-18 was 0 bbl of oil and 0 Mscf of gas, with 0 hours of uptime.

## Status
The incident record is closed as of 2026-08-22. The well remains shut in until the workover.

## Next actions
- An ESP replacement workover is planned to start on 2026-08-23 (EV-0156).
- The Production Engineer will review the teardown findings once the unit is out of the hole.
- Post-workover rates are to be compared with the baseline above.

No specific procedure is referenced for this incident.

chunks.section: Diagnosis: reading VSD trip codes, phase currents and downhole sensor data
chunks.text:
1. Read pump intake pressure, discharge pressure, motor winding temperature, intake temperature and vibration if available.
2. A falling intake pressure with falling current points to drawdown or gas. A rising motor temperature before the trip points to heat, poor cooling or a developing electrical fault.
3. Loss of sensor signal together with a ground fault or imbalance trip is a strong sign of a cable or motor failure.
4. Compare with the last stable values and with the trend over the previous 24 hours, not only with the last reading.

### 4. Classify

Classify the trip as one of: surface or supply cause, process or flowline cause, fluid or gas related, or suspected downhole electrical or mechanical fault. This class decides the restart route.

## Megger and insulation resistance checks

Only competent electrical personnel carry out the test, under a valid permit to work and with the HSE Advisor satisfied that isolation is in place.

1. Isolate and lock out the VSD. Prove dead. Disconnect the output to the cable at the VSD or junction box, so that the drive is not exposed to test voltage.
2. Discharge the cable to earth before and after the test.
3. Use a megger at the voltage specified for the cable and motor system. Test phase to earth for each phase, and between phases where the instrument allows.
4. Apply the test voltage for 60 seconds and record the value, the time, the temperature and the instrument used.
5. Judge the results:
   - 100 megohm or more: good.
   - Between 10 and 100 megohm: marginal. Record the value, check for moisture at the junction box, and retest. Restart only with Production Engineer approval and close monitoring.
   - Below 10 megohm: failed. Do not restart.
   - Large differences between phases, or a reading that falls steadily during the test, point to a developing fault even when the value looks acceptable.
6. Test at the surface cable end first. If the surface cable and junction box are clean and dry, a low reading means the fault is downhole.
7. Restore the connections, remove the locks and close the permit only after the test sheet is signed.

answer.answer: It was not a one-off: W-09, a Dune Field well, failed in October 2025 and W-27, a Wadi Field well, in August 2026. Both ran pumps from batch 7Q-0419, like W-17's pump [1][2][3]. chunks_sent.title: SOP-OPS-001 ESP Trip Response and Restart
chunks_sent.section: Diagnosis: reading VSD trip codes, phase currents and downhole sensor data
chunks_sent.text:
1. Read pump intake pressure, discharge pressure, motor winding temperature, intake temperature and vibration if available.
2. A falling intake pressure with falling current points to drawdown or gas. A rising motor temperature before the trip points to heat, poor cooling or a developing electrical fault.
3. Loss of sensor signal together with a ground fault or imbalance trip is a strong sign of a cable or motor failure.
4. Compare with the last stable values and with the trend over the previous 24 hours, not only with the last reading.

### 4. Classify

Classify the trip as one of: surface or supply cause, process or flowline cause, fluid or gas related, or suspected downhole electrical or mechanical fault. This class decides the restart route.

chunks_sent.title: SOP-OPS-001 ESP Trip Response and Restart
chunks_sent.text:
## Megger and insulation resistance checks

Only competent electrical personnel carry out the test, under a valid permit to work and with the HSE Advisor satisfied that isolation is in place.

1. Isolate and lock out the VSD. Prove dead. Disconnect the output to the cable at the VSD or junction box, so that the drive is not exposed to test voltage.
2. Discharge the cable to earth before and after the test.
3. Use a megger at the voltage specified for the cable and motor system. Test phase to earth for each phase, and between phases where the instrument allows.
4. Apply the test voltage for 60 seconds and record the value, the time, the temperature and the instrument used.
5. Judge the results:
   - 100 megohm or more: good.
   - Between 10 and 100 megohm: marginal. Record the value, check for moisture at the junction box, and retest. Restart only with Production Engineer approval and close monitoring.
   - Below 10 megohm: failed. Do not restart.
   - Large differences between phases, or a reading that falls steadily during the test, point to a developing fault even when the value looks acceptable.
6. Test at the surface cable end first. If the surface cable and junction box are clean and dry, a low reading means the fault is downhole.
7. Restore the connections, remove the locks and close the permit only after the test sheet is signed.
